name: Google tag (gtag.js)
plain: Google's page script for analytics and ads; sets IDs like _ga and _gcl_au in the browser.
meaning: _ga (2 years, capped at 400 days in Chrome) joins visits into one user, _gid lasts 24 hours, _gcl_au 90 days for ad conversions. Consent Mode v2 changes what is sent if the person declines.

access.persistence: _ga about 2 years (400 days in Chrome), _gid 24 hours, _gcl_au 90 days
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

chrome.note: Script runs in any browser, cookie lifetimes vary

limits.headline: Can tell Google about your visits and actions on a site that uses the tag
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you open a page with the Google tag
can: Set IDs such as _ga and _gcl_au in your browser
Report page views, clicks and purchases to Google
Link visits over time with the same ID
Feed Google Analytics and Google Ads
cannot: Run on sites that do not include the tag
See other sites unless they also use it
Keep the ID if you clear cookies or block the script
Know your name unless you sign in to Google or the site shares it
limits.differs: Safari and Firefox limit how long some of its cookies last. Chrome keeps them for longer.

story.what_it_is: Google's page script for analytics and ads that sets IDs in your browser.

marketing.name: Google tag cookies
marketing.pitch: Google documents the cookies like _ga that its tag sets to measure visits and ad results.

story.for_you: You do not see the script. It sets small files like _ga that tell Google you are the same visitor, and counts what you do. If you decline cookies, Consent Mode can still send limited signals.
story.for_makers: The Google tag is the base for Analytics and Google Ads on a large share of the web. It counts visits, sales and ad clicks in one tool. Consent Mode lets sites model results when people say no.

use_cases.example: A blog owner sees how many people visited today, which pages they read and where they came from.
A shop sees which Google ad made each sale, using the _gcl cookies and click IDs.
A browser game site sees how many players come from a search, and how long they stay.
A retailer builds a remarketing list of people who looked at a product.
A news site measures which stories keep readers longest, to decide what to write.
Consent Mode sends pings with no cookies if a person declines, which Google uses to model the missing data.

risks: Google sees data from huge number of sites

technical_bounds: Safari caps JS set cookies at 7 days
Consent Mode modelling fills gaps for declined users

abuse: Cross-site ad profiles and remarketing lists

history.change: Consent Mode v2 required for EEA ad personalisation from Mar 2024
Universal Analytics stopped processing; GA4 only
